items.title: Jane Ira Bloom interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 3, 1998
items.q: I corresponded with him for years. And eventually our correspondence came up with the idea of how about commissioning the first musician... to be part of this NASA art program.

ctx.x: I wrote a letter to NASA in the early 80s. I was just fascinated with whether NASA had ever thought about the future of the arts in space. I was very interested in what zero gravity might mean to the future of artistic performance. You know if there wasn’t gravity, how might music and dance and sculpture and theater, how all these things might be different. So I wondered whether NASA might have ever thought about it too. I wrote them a letter and six months later I got an envelope back from a gentleman named…

the various NASA facilities, to see things people never get to see. And it was an extraordinary experience. And from that experience you contribute a work of art to their traveling space art collection. And I wound up composing a piece for chamber orchestra and jazz musicians that got performed at the Kennedy Space Center in 1989, and involved six jazz musicians inside the orchestra, it involved live electronics that I used, and a sound surround speaker system. So it had all kinds of interesting new elements to…
